findings.description: A long-lived AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext as Lambda environment variables in the Terraform source. They are exposed in version control, in Terraform state, and to any principal with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration or console read access.

No kms_key_arn is set, so the environment variables holding these secrets are protected only by the default AWS-managed Lambda key, with no customer-managed key policy to restrict which principals can decrypt them. Given the secrets present, this materially widens who can read them.

The function targets the nodejs12.x runtime, which has reached end of life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving the execution environment exposed to unpatched vulnerabilities in the runtime and its bundled libraries.

The lambda.amazonaws.com service trust policy has no aws:SourceAccount or aws:SourceArn condition scoping which account or function ARN may assume the role. This is a defence-in-depth gap against service confused-deputy patterns.
